title: A giant rotating wheel lifts boats between Scottish canals
body: Scotland's **Falkirk Wheel** carries boats in two water-filled chambers, raising one while lowering the other. A floating boat displaces its own weight in water, so adding a boat lets an equal weight of water leave the chamber. With water levels carefully controlled, the two sides remain balanced. Gears keep the chambers level while the wheel turns, so the boats stay afloat throughout the ride.

slides.heading: The boat replaces water
slides.text: A 10-tonne floating boat displaces 10 tonnes of water. At the same water level, a chamber with the boat can weigh the same as that chamber filled with water alone.

slides.heading: From one level to another
items: A boat enters a water-filled chamber.
The gates close and the balanced wheel rotates.
Gears keep the chamber level as the boat rises or descends.

slides.heading: Balance saves effort
slides.text: The descending side helps counterbalance the rising side. Motors still supply energy to turn the mechanism, but they do not have to lift an unbalanced load of boats and water.

slides.heading: Boat lifts around the world: how far each raises a boat, in metres
slides.note: Anderton opened in 1875, Falkirk and Strépy-Thieu in 2002, the Three Gorges ship lift in 2016
slides.explanation: The Falkirk Wheel’s 24 m is modest: Strépy-Thieu in Belgium lifts boats 73 m, and the ship lift at China’s Three Gorges Dam 113 m.

slides.question: Why does adding a boat not unbalance the wheel?
options: It displaces its own weight in water
Pumps add water to the other side
Boats are weighed and matched up
Motors hold the heavy side up
slides.explanation: A floating boat displaces its own weight in water, so adding one lets an equal weight of water leave the chamber and the two sides stay balanced.
